title: Development spending hits record low 6.53% in July to October
excerpt: Ministries spent Tk 20,160 crore of a Tk 3.09 lakh crore ADP in four months. Health and disaster relief spending is among the weakest.
content:
Government ministries spent only 6.53 percent of this year's Annual Development Programme (ADP) in the first four months of the 2026-27 fiscal year, according to data from the Implementation Monitoring and Evaluation Division (IMED). The Business Standard called it a record low, while Prothom Alo said it was the lowest in five years.

Spending from July to October came to Tk 20,160 crore against a target of Tk 3.09 lakh crore, The Business Standard reported. The rate was 8.33 percent in the same period last year. Spending of foreign-funded project money fell to 5.52 percent, from 9.16 percent a year earlier.

Where spending stalled

  • Health Education and Family Welfare Division: 2.88 percent
  • Health Services Division: 3.94 percent
  • Disaster Management and Relief Ministry: 1 percent or less (Prothom Alo)
  • Foreign Affairs Ministry (Tk 1.85 billion allocated) and Chittagong Hill Tracts Affairs Ministry (Tk 9.56 billion across 10 projects): nothing spent (Prothom Alo)
  • Primary and Mass Education Ministry: 24.15 percent, among the better performers

Mustafa K Mujeri, executive director of the Institute for Inclusive Finance and Development, told The Business Standard that shortages of funds were behind the slow spending.

Why it matters

Slow development spending delays hospitals, disaster shelters and other public works that NGOs often build on or fill gaps around. The weak use of foreign-funded money also matters for donor-backed projects, where NGOs are often implementing partners. A rush to spend late in the year can also lead to poor-quality work.

What to watch

Whether the government trims the ADP in its mid-year revision, and whether health and disaster spending picks up during the dry season, when most construction happens.
